gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-n: Noto Znamenny Musical Notation keeps its stroke endings well back from the stems. Nixie One above it draws retro-tech curves like cut ribbon of constant width, so the heading feels nostalgic while the sans-serif text stays modern.
gen-nixie-one-gf-sansation: Sansation reads approachable and smooth, its curves turning inward without any pooling of ink at the joins. Nixie One adds a nostalgic, unmodulated line that gives the pair its edge.
gen-nixie-one-gf-sarabun: Retro wire meets open, friendly text: Nixie One draws true monoline curves with clear gaps. And Sarabun opens a wide channel into every bowl, which is the pair's most winning quality.
gen-nixie-one-gf-spinnaker: Wire-thin nostalgia meets a modern text face, with Nixie One drawing every curve in a single thickness and open gaps. Spinnaker keeps its counters connected to the outside, giving the pair its openness.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Nostalgic wire-like curves from Nixie One run from top to baseline in one constant stroke, with clear gaps. Below, Tsukimi Rounded gives it round, parallel-edged sans-serif forms to rest against.
gen-nixie-one-gf-urbanist: Retro wire, then a pen-drawn modern: Nixie One keeps its curves open and its stroke constant. But Urbanist, a sans with a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, gives the heading a contemporary partner.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-truculenta: Cut-out fun, letters pinned far apart: Press Start 2P is the retro half. And Truculenta, plain sans with a compact line, gives that loose spacing a tight, approachable counterweight.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-victor-mono: Press Start 2P pins its cut-out letters far apart, loud and retro. Victor Mono, a monospace with bowls left open on one side and loose spacing, adds a precise, structured counterpoint.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-voces: Big-bowled retro fun with light modulation: that is Press Start 2P up top. And Voces, plain sans built tall with close stem-to-hairline ratios, keeps that fun grounded and professional.
gen-righteous-gf-carlito: Thin steel rod, bent into bowls that fill the line. Righteous is built for commanding display, while Carlito, a sans-serif with open round letters, does its best work at small sizes.
